validity.researcher_notes: The brief's own source ladder already tells me this was settled by the annual leg and not to re-derive it — confirmed by reading batches/india-gas/staging/annual/rows/P0928.json directly. That leg found, with 2+ independent sources (Enerdata 2016-08-17 and The Daily Star 2016-08-16, both independently reporting the same Economic Times original): 'Thirteen routes with a total length of about 6,900 km of pipelines have been proposed' under India's 2016 Hydrocarbon Vision 2030 — i.e. 6,900 km is the SUM across 13 separate proposed domestic/regional pipelines (most of them wholly inside India, e.g. the Contai-Haldia-Duttapulia line named in the same source), not the length of any single India-Myanmar-Bangladesh line. No source anywhere gives a length for one cross-border pipeline; the most current evidence (Prothom Alo, 2026-08-04, on this month's revived Bangladesh-Myanmar pipeline talks) explicitly states the route itself remains undetermined. So the length_ratio flag's implicit question — 'is the drawn 893 km route wrong, or is 6900 km wrong?' — has one clean answer: 6,900 km is not this pipeline's length at all, it is a mis-attributed multi-route program total (traced by the annual leg to GEM's own wiki page borrowing the Hydrocarbon Vision 2030 total and presenting it as this single row's LengthKnown). I am not independently re-verifying the 893 km drawn route's accuracy — with no real target length existing yet for a single line, there is nothing to ratio-check it against, and proposing new route coordinates is out of scope. Not staging a fill (the recommended action, blanking LengthKnownKm, was already the annual leg's finding); this entry exists so the length_ratio flag specifically closes with a documented answer rather than being silently dropped.
